interaction: Hash navigation works locally and on GitHub Pages, including direct opening and browser back/forward.
The canvas remains mounted; page navigation preserves images, workflows, viewport and undo history. Hidden canvas shortcuts and clipboard interception are suspended.
Regular and lingerie modes have independent in-memory drafts, preserved when returning to the canvas.
The regular mode starts with the original Figma garment example. Lingerie starts empty.
Garments support choosing assets, local batch upload through AssetPicker and direct file drop, at most four images. File types and 20MB limit use the existing readImage validation.
Clothing category, automatic flat-lay switch, single/multiple task choice, description/reference/model-set tabs, aspect ratio and generation speed retain local selections.
Descriptions support up to 2000 characters, expanded editing, clear and clipboard copy. Reference mode accepts one model image; model-set mode accepts four.
Generate validates clothing, categories and the active model input, then explains that the AI service is not connected. No artificial history, generated image, charge or live task is created.
The design's internal annotation in the description field is replaced with a product-facing input placeholder.
At narrow widths the form and history stack vertically; short desktop windows scroll the form while keeping generation controls accessible.
validation: Read live Figma design context and shared source components. Per user instruction, no browser, test, build or visual verification was run.
